proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(N=3n\).  By \(\textup{def:projected-experiment}\), concatenating \(D_K,D_D,D_A\) identifies \(Q_P\) with \(P^{\otimes N}\).  Hence an interval measurable in the three evaluation folds is an interval in the \(N\)-observation experiment.

We first prove the nuisance-product lower bound on every positive-product index.  Put
\[
 a_N=\frac{\varepsilon_{g,n}}{K},
 \qquad
 b_N=\frac{\varepsilon_{q,n}}{KA}.
\]
Because \(A\) and \(K\) are fixed positive constants, the assumed product condition gives
\[
 a_Nb_N
 =\frac{\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}}{K^2A}
 =o\!\left((\log N)^{-1/2}\right).
\]
Condition \((\mathrm{CT2})\) permits the invocation of \(\textup{lem:jms-support-localized-product-benchmark}\) with supplied source fit \((\widehat g,\widehat q/A)\), source radii \((a_N,b_N)\), and \(s=8\).  This is an assumed conditional transfer of the cited support; it is not inferred from a lower bound over an unspecified larger source class.

The source's recentering step moves a bounded center inward by at most half of each nuisance radius and uses a half-radius construction around the recentered pair; the triangle inequality then keeps that entire construction in the original radius ball.  Consequently, \((\mathrm{CT2})\) does not require \(\|\widehat g\|_\infty\) or \(\|\widehat q\|_\infty\) to be a small multiple of \(C_{\mathrm{env}}\), nor does it separately require \(\varepsilon_{g,n}+\varepsilon_{q,n}\to0\).  Some compatibility premise nevertheless cannot be removed from this proof: \(\textup{def:supplied-fit-set}\) gives only \(L^8(P_X)\) control, which neither supplies the pointwise bounded center required by construction (44) nor guarantees that the displayed supremum contains any law for an arbitrary external fit pair.  Condition \((\mathrm{CT2})\) states exactly the support inclusion used below.

To track the outcome rescaling, let \(\widehat\theta\) be an arbitrary estimator in the transformed experiment and define the source-scale estimator
\[
 \widehat\vartheta_R(z_1,\ldots,z_N)
 =A^{-1}\widehat\theta\bigl(S_Az_1,\ldots,S_Az_N\bigr).
\]
Take \(\gamma=3/4\), which is larger than \(\alpha\) because \(\alpha<1/2\).  The cited lemma supplies an \(R\) in one of its two fuzzy supports such that
\[
 R^{\otimes N}\!\left\{
 |\widehat\vartheta_R-\vartheta(R)|
 \ge c_\gamma a_Nb_N
 \left(\frac{\log(1/a_N)}{\log N}\right)^3
 \right\}\ge\gamma .
\]
Let \(P=R\circ S_A^{-1}\).  By \((\mathrm{CT2})\), \(P\in\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\), the supplied pair is in \(\mathcal H_n(P)\), and \(\theta_0(P)=A\vartheta(R)\).  Since \(S_A\) is a measurable bijection, the preceding display is exactly
\[
 Q_P\!\left\{
 |\widehat\theta-\theta_0(P)|
 \ge c_\gamma A a_Nb_N
 \left(\frac{\log(1/a_N)}{\log N}\right)^3
 \right\}\ge\gamma .
\]
Notice that the source outcome radius used here is \(b_N=\varepsilon_{q,n}/(KA)\), so the source separation is multiplied by \(A\) only after the pushforward.  In particular,
\[
 A a_Nb_N
 =\frac{\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}}{K^2}.
\]

Let \(\ell_n=1\vee\log(1/\varepsilon_{g,n})\).  Since \(0<\varepsilon_{g,n}\le C_{\mathrm{env}}\) on a positive-product index and \(K\ge e(1\vee C_{\mathrm{env}})\),
\[
 \log(1/a_N)=\log(K/\varepsilon_{g,n})\ge\ell_n.
\]
Moreover, \(\log(3n)\le c_0\log(en)\) for a universal \(c_0\).  It follows from \(\textup{def:rate-scales}\) that
\[
 A a_Nb_N
 \left(\frac{\log(1/a_N)}{\log N}\right)^3
 \ge c_1\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}
 \min\!\left\{1,
 \left(\frac{\ell_n}{\log(en)}\right)^3\right\}
 =c_1\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\Lambda_n,
\]
where \(c_1>0\) depends only on \(C_{\mathrm{env}}\) and \(c_\xi\) through \(A\) and \(K\).  Thus every estimator has, on a law in the transferred fuzzy support, error at least \(c_2\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\Lambda_n\) with probability at least \(\gamma\).

Every transferred support law lies in \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\subseteq\mathcal G_n\subseteq\mathcal U_n\), and its supplied pair lies in \(\mathcal H_n(P)\), by \((\mathrm{CT2})\), \(\textup{def:gaussian-nondegenerate-subclass}\), and \(\textup{def:honesty-union}\).  Union honesty therefore implies honesty over this support.  Applying \(\textup{lem:honest-interval-length-reduction}\) with \(r=c_2\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\Lambda_n\), \(\beta=\gamma\), and the class equal to the transferred fuzzy support yields
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal G_{\xi,n}:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}
 E_{Q_P}|C_n|
 \ge c_3\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\Lambda_n.
\]
When \(\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}=0\), this display remains true because its right-hand side is zero, and no fuzzy-support transfer is invoked.

We next prove the parametric lower bound by a distinct two-point construction.  Fix
\[
 \beta=\frac{\alpha+1/2}{2},
 \qquad \alpha<\beta<1/2.
\]
Use the covariate law and anchor regressions in \((\mathrm{CT1})\).  For \(j\in\{0,1\}\), set \(v_0=0\), \(v_1=\Delta=hN^{-1/2}\), and let \(P_j=P_{n,v_j}\), where \(h>0\) will be fixed below.  Taking \(h\le h_0\) ensures \(|v_j|\le h_0\).  The equations in \((\mathrm{CT1})\) give
\[
 Y=v_jT+\{q_{*,n}(X)-v_jg_{*,n}(X)\}+A\zeta.
\]
Thus \(\theta_0(P_j)=v_j\), \(f_{0,j}=q_{*,n}-v_jg_{*,n}\), and \(\xi_j=A\zeta\).  In particular,
\[
 E_{P_j}[\xi_j\mid X,T]=0,
 \qquad
 E_{P_j}[\xi_j^2\mid X,T]=A^2\ge c_\xi.
\]
Condition \((\mathrm{CT1})\) supplies the remaining envelope, Gaussian-branch, and supplied-fit membership conditions, so \(P_j\in\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\) and \((\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P_j)\).

Under \(P_0\), conditional division of the two Gaussian outcome densities gives the one-observation likelihood ratio
\[
 L=\frac{dP_1}{dP_0}
 =\exp\!\left\{
 \frac{\Delta\eta\{Y-q_{*,n}(X)\}}{A^2}
 -\frac{\Delta^2\eta^2}{2A^2}
 \right\}.
\]
Under \(P_0\), \(\{Y-q_{*,n}(X)\}/A=\zeta\) is standard Gaussian and independent of \(\eta\).  Its moment-generating function gives
\[
 E_{P_0}[L^2\mid X,\eta]
 =\exp(\Delta^2\eta^2/A^2).
\]
Since \(\eta\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), direct Gaussian integration yields
\[
 E_{P_0}[L^2]
 =\left(1-\frac{2\Delta^2}{A^2}\right)^{-1/2}.
\]
Independence of the \(N\) observations consequently gives
\[
 \chi^2\!\left(P_1^{\otimes N},P_0^{\otimes N}\right)
 =\left(1-\frac{2h^2}{A^2N}\right)^{-N/2}-1.
\]
If \(2h^2/A^2\le1/2\), then \(-\log(1-x)\le2x\) for \(0\le x\le1/2\) implies
\[
 \chi^2\!\left(P_1^{\otimes N},P_0^{\otimes N}\right)
 \le \exp(2h^2/A^2)-1.
\]
Choose \(h>0\), depending only on \(\alpha\), \(A\), and \(h_0\), small enough that the last expression is at most \(4(1-2\beta)^2\).  Cauchy--Schwarz then gives
\[
 \left\|P_1^{\otimes N}-P_0^{\otimes N}\right\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 =\frac12E_{P_0^{\otimes N}}|L_N-1|
 \le\frac12\sqrt{\chi^2(P_1^{\otimes N},P_0^{\otimes N})}
 \le1-2\beta.
\]

For an arbitrary estimator \(\widehat\theta\), the events
\[
 A_j=\{|\widehat\theta-v_j|<\Delta/2\},\qquad j\in\{0,1\},
\]
are disjoint.  Therefore
\[
 P_0^{\otimes N}(A_0)+P_1^{\otimes N}(A_1)
 \le P_0^{\otimes N}(A_0)+P_0^{\otimes N}(A_1)
 +\|P_1^{\otimes N}-P_0^{\otimes N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le1+\|P_1^{\otimes N}-P_0^{\otimes N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}},
\]
and hence
\[
 \max_{j\in\{0,1\}}
 P_j^{\otimes N}\!\left\{
 |\widehat\theta-v_j|\ge\frac{h}{2\sqrt N}
 \right\}
 \ge\frac{1-\|P_1^{\otimes N}-P_0^{\otimes N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}}{2}
 \ge\beta.
\]
The two laws are in the honesty union and are compatible with the supplied fits by \((\mathrm{CT1})\).  A second application of \(\textup{lem:honest-interval-length-reduction}\), now with the class \(\{P_0,P_1\}\), yields
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal G_{\xi,n}:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}
 E_{Q_P}|C_n|\ge c_4N^{-1/2}\ge c_5n^{-1/2}.
\]

The same supremum is bounded below by both the parametric and nuisance-product terms.  Therefore \(\max\{x,y\}\ge(x+y)/2\) and \(\textup{def:rate-scales}\) give
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal G_{\xi,n}:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}
 E_{Q_P}|C_n|
 \ge c\left\{n^{-1/2}+
 \varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\Lambda_n\right\}
 =c d_n^-.
\]
Finally, \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\subseteq\mathcal G_n\) and \(\textup{def:length-vector}\) imply \(L_G(C_n)\ge c d_n^-\).  The proof used the conditional outcome-variance restriction and the two transfer conditions only for these lower-bound subexperiments.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(\gamma\in(1/2,1)\), \(1\le s\le\infty\), and constants \(C_\theta,C_g,C_q>0\).  Consider the Gaussian-treatment partially linear construction (44) of Jin, Mackey, and Syrgkanis with treatment-noise variance one, a fixed supplied center \(\bar h_N=(\bar g_N,\bar q_N)\) satisfying \(\|\bar g_N\|_\infty\le C_g\) and \(\|\bar q_N\|_\infty\le C_q\), and nuisance radii \(a_N,b_N>0\).  Let \(\mathfrak S_N(a_N,b_N;\bar h_N)\) be the particular support of laws \(R_{\lambda,\rho}\) generated in (44): each such law obeys
\[
 T=g_R(X)+\eta,\qquad
 Y=\vartheta(R)T+f_R(X)+\xi,\qquad
 \eta\mid X\sim\mathcal N(0,1),\qquad
 E_R[\xi\mid X,T]=0,
\]
has \(|\vartheta(R)|\le C_\theta\), \(\|g_R\|_\infty\le C_g\), and \(\|q_R\|_\infty\le C_q\), where \(q_R(x)=E_R[Y\mid X=x]\), and satisfies
\[
 \|g_R-\bar g_N\|_{L^s(R_X)}\le a_N,
 \qquad
 \|q_R-\bar q_N\|_{L^s(R_X)}\le b_N.
\]
Assume that the bounded-center recentering described immediately before construction (44) makes this support well defined.  If \(a_Nb_N=o((\log N)^{-1/2})\), the two moment-matched priors \(\nu_{0,N},\nu_{1,N}\) used in Appendix D are supported on \(\mathfrak S_N(a_N,b_N;\bar h_N)\) and have the following support-localized consequence: for every estimator \(\widehat\vartheta\) based on \(N\) observations, for all sufficiently large \(N\), there are \(i\in\{0,1\}\) and \(R\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu_{i,N})\) such that
\[
 R^{\otimes N}\!\left\{
 |\widehat\vartheta-\vartheta(R)|
 \ge c_\gamma a_Nb_N
 \left(\frac{\log(1/a_N)}{\log N}\right)^3
 \right\}\ge\gamma .
\]
This is only the nuisance-product conclusion obtained from their fuzzy supports in equation (56); it does not include the separate \(N^{-1/2}\) mechanism of their equations (57)--(58).

source.locator: Theorem 3.2 and Appendix D, especially construction (44), the moment-matched priors from (41)--(43), and equations (55)--(56)

attestation.note: Checked against the arXiv v3 PDF.  Appendix D derives the nuisance-product term in equation (56) from the two displayed fuzzy priors; the separate parametric term is introduced only afterward in equations (57)--(58).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Fix a deterministic sequence of supplied pairs \((\widehat g,\widehat q)\), and set \(N=3n\).  Suppose that
\[
 \varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}
 =o\!\left((\log(3n))^{-1/2}\right)
\]
along the indices for which \(\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}>0\).  Assume the following conditional-transfer compatibility condition.  There are constants \(A=A(C_{\mathrm{env}},c_\xi)>0\), \(K=K(C_{\mathrm{env}},c_\xi)\ge e(1\vee C_{\mathrm{env}})\), and \(h_0=h_0(C_{\mathrm{env}},c_\xi)>0\), independent of \(n\), with \(A^2\ge c_\xi\), such that:

\(\mathrm{CT1}\) for every sufficiently large \(n\), there are a covariate law \(P_{X,n}\) and measurable functions \(g_{*,n},q_{*,n}\) for which, for every \(|v|\le h_0\), the law \(P_{n,v}\) defined by
\[
 X\sim P_{X,n},\qquad
 T=g_{*,n}(X)+\eta,\qquad
 Y=q_{*,n}(X)+v\eta+A\zeta,
 \qquad \eta,\zeta\stackrel{\mathrm{ind}}{\sim}\mathcal N(0,1),
\]
with \((\eta,\zeta)\perp X\), belongs to \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\) and satisfies \((\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P_{n,v})\);

\(\mathrm{CT2}\) whenever \(\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}>0\), the fixed source center \((\widehat g,\widehat q/A)\) and radii
\[
 a_N=\frac{\varepsilon_{g,n}}{K},
 \qquad
 b_N=\frac{\varepsilon_{q,n}}{KA}
\]
satisfy the hypotheses of \(\textup{lem:jms-support-localized-product-benchmark}\), and the measurable outcome-rescaling map \(S_A(x,t,y)=(x,t,Ay)\) sends every law \(R\) in the two cited fuzzy supports to \(P=R\circ S_A^{-1}\in\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\) with \((\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)\) and \(\theta_0(P)=A\vartheta(R)\).

Then there exists \(c>0\), depending only on \(\alpha\), \(C_{\mathrm{env}}\), and \(c_\xi\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), every interval \(C_n\) satisfying
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal U_n:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}
 Q_P\{\theta_0\in C_n\}\ge1-\alpha
\]
also satisfies
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal G_{\xi,n}:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}
 E_{Q_P}|C_n|\ge c d_n^- ,
\]
and therefore \(L_G(C_n)\ge c d_n^-\).  The conditional variance restriction defining \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\), as well as \((\mathrm{CT1})\)--\((\mathrm{CT2})\), is confined to this Gaussian lower-bound subexperiment and is not a hypothesis of the adaptive upper-frontier theorem.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The unconditional frozen claim is not justified for an arbitrary fixed supplied pair: its compatible Gaussian subexperiment may be empty, and the cited class-level minimax theorem does not itself put the bad law inside whichever fuzzy support one tries to embed.  The proposed claim narrows only to an explicit conditional-transfer/interiority premise.  That premise asserts support membership and a nonempty compatible parametric path, but does not assume target separation, testing affinity, or the desired length bound; those are supplied respectively by the support-localized cited result and the two-point calculation.  The source is invoked before rescaling at outcome center \(\widehat q/A\) and radius \(\varepsilon_{q,n}/(KA)\).

proposed.justification: It gives the certified Gaussian coordinate on every supplied-fit sequence for which the published fuzzy support and a nonempty Gaussian two-point path transfer into the projected model.
proposed.gap: The conclusion is conditional on explicit fit-support compatibility, and the certified nuisance-product coordinate retains the published logarithmic factor.  Neither unconditional transfer for arbitrary supplied fits nor a full \(d_n\) lower bound is established.
proposed.consumer: It prevents shortening of the Gaussian coordinate below \(d_n^-\) on the stated transfer-compatible subexperiment and thereby supplies the certified obstruction relevant to union-honest intervals.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The narrowed claim introduces the exact conditional-transfer premises and replaces the overbroad cited benchmark by its support-localized nuisance-product version; the dependency and free-symbol metadata must change with it.

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.2 combines two distinct Gaussian mechanisms: Appendix D equation (56) obtains only the nuisance-product term with its logarithmic factor from moment-matched fuzzy supports, while equations (57)--(58) supply the separate parametric term.  Theorem 5.4 gives a fixed-positive-cumulant ACE point-estimation upper bound on a separate class.
proposed.matched_by: The conditionally transferred Gaussian-coordinate theorem and Open-ended Questions 7--9

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 and Proposition 2 characterize expected-length adaptation over unions in Gaussian linear-functional experiments.
The paper obtains composite-hypothesis lower bounds by moment-matched priors and chi-square control of normal mixtures.
Theorem 5 rules out second-order PLM orthogonality under Gaussian residuals, while Theorems 8--10 construct higher-order moments under non-Gaussian residuals.
Theorem 2 establishes coverage and interval-length control for the filtered union, while Theorem 3 supplies the oracle-proximity and existence ingredient.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The prior comparator row incorrectly suggested that the fuzzy support itself supplies the complete Gaussian rate.  The replacement records the source's separate nuisance-product and parametric mechanisms.

prose_updates.tldr: For a primitive JMS partially linear law and fixed training-realized nuisance fits supplied within stated \(L^8(P_X)\) radii, one interval is honest over exact-Gaussian and shrinking fourth-cumulant-separated branches of the projected evaluation experiment. Four explicit Bonferroni-calibrated median-of-means events use nonempty finite-sample block partitions and cover safe DML, four residual moments, centered Appell inversion, and its empirical slope. The non-Gaussian finite-sample length is \(\min\{d_n,B_n/\delta_n+d_np_{\mathrm{sel},n}\}\), with an explicit bound on \(p_{\mathrm{sel},n}\), and reduces to \(\min\{d_n,B_n/\delta_n\}\) when \(\delta_n/s_n\to\infty\). On supplied-fit sequences satisfying the stated conditional-transfer compatibility, the certified Gaussian lower coordinate is \(d_n^-\): the nuisance-product/log term comes from the transferred JMS fuzzy support, while \(n^{-1/2}\) comes from a separate compatible two-point family. Conditional outcome-noise nondegeneracy is confined to that lower subexperiment. The fuzzy-Hermite branchwise converse and removal of the Gaussian logarithm remain open-ended questions.

project_justification.fill: The proved upper component combines explicit nonempty-block four-event calibration, a finite-sample branch-selection error envelope, a safe unnormalized DML interval, and a fully centered split Appell inversion. The Gaussian converse is certified at \(d_n^-\) only under explicit conditional transfer of the published fuzzy supports and a compatible nonempty two-point path; its fuzzy and parametric mechanisms are kept separate. Conditional outcome-noise nondegeneracy is auxiliary to that lower subexperiment, and the cross-branch PLM-compatible fuzzy-Hermite converse remains open.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The statistical law class contains only primitive laws. The selected training-realized functions are external fixed inputs, and the upper theorem is uniform over all supplied pairs in \(\mathcal H_n(P)\). The Gaussian-coordinate converse is narrower: it applies to supplied-fit sequences for which the stated source fuzzy supports and a nonempty Gaussian two-point path transfer into the same projected class.

prose_updates.related_work: Jin, Mackey, and Syrgkanis inform two separate pieces of the Gaussian coordinate: their Appendix D equation (56) derives the nuisance-product term with its logarithmic factor from moment-matched fuzzy supports, whereas equations (57)--(58) derive the parametric term from a Gaussian two-point model. The present theorem transfers the first piece only conditionally on exact support compatibility and independently proves the second on a compatible embedded path; it does not attribute arbitrary-fit support localization to their theorem. Their Theorem 5.4 informs the fixed-separation ACE component but does not give a union-honest shrinking-cumulant interval. The auxiliary condition \(E_P[\xi^2\mid X,T]\ge c_{\xi}\) is not attributed to their envelope and is used only for the Gaussian expected-length lower subexperiment. Mackey, Syrgkanis, and Zadik, Theorems 5 and 8--10, inform the Gaussian obstruction and higher-order score. Cai and Low, Theorem 1 and Proposition 2, inform branchwise expected length, while their Gaussian model has no learned PLM residual. Cai and Low's 2011 Hermite mixture method informs the fuzzy-prior handle. Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman inform localized product-mixture calculations. Chernozhukov et al. supply the split DML benchmark. Zheng, Bonvini, and Guo's Theorem 2 informs filtered-union coverage and interval-length control, while their Theorem 3 supplies the oracle-proximity and existence ingredient; neither theorem uses treatment cumulants. The sibling repository paper \(\texttt{stat\_sa\_plm\_cumulant\_converse}\) proves fixed-separation spectral and estimation constructions and explicitly leaves shrinking separation, adaptive switching, uniform inference, and a local matching lower bound unresolved. The present proved contribution is the conditional supplied-fit shrinking-separation upper frontier together with the conditional Gaussian coordinate just described; it does not claim a matching Pareto frontier. Quessy and Mailhot analyze centered and studentized normality statistics without nuisance-contaminated residuals. Armstrong, Kline, and Sun motivate caution about pretesting for a different point-risk object.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The certified Gaussian lower coordinate is \(d_n^-\), not \(d_n\), and is conditional on two explicit compatibility requirements: transfer of the support-localized JMS fuzzy priors after outcome rescaling, and existence of a nonempty Gaussian two-point path around a compatible anchor. The cited fuzzy support supplies only the nuisance-product/log term; the parametric term is proved separately. The auxiliary subclass \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\) is used only for this converse. The upper theorem needs none of these lower-experiment restrictions and does not identify a matching Pareto boundary. Its finite-sample guarantee starts at \(n=\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\), when every requested calibration block count is available. The early kill test remains a finite Rademacher-partition exponential-Hermite pair supported on primitive PLM laws, sharing admissible fixed supplied fits, and inducing projected mixtures with bounded chi-square distance and the target displacements in the open-ended question.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The law class is primitive and contains no learner-performance condition. All upper-frontier inference is conditional on fixed supplied fits and uniform over their radius set. The Appell polynomial estimates the first four raw residual moments on a fold independent of inversion. Every median-of-means operator partitions the sample into \(b_n(\beta)=\min\{n,\lceil8\log(2/\beta)\rceil\}\) nonempty blocks, and the upper theorem assumes \(n\ge\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\). Four named events receive error \(\alpha/4\) each, while the separate bound \(p_{\mathrm{sel},n}\) quantifies wrong-branch selection. The Gaussian lower theorem is explicitly conditional: for positive nuisance-product indices, the source is invoked with treatment radius \(\varepsilon_{g,n}/K\), outcome fit \(\widehat q/A\), and outcome radius \(\varepsilon_{q,n}/(KA)\), then pushed forward by \(S_A(x,t,y)=(x,t,Ay)\); a separate compatible two-point path supplies \(n^{-1/2}\). The novel restriction \(E_P[\xi^2\mid X,T]\ge c_{\xi}\) defines only \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\) and is used only in that converse. The sibling repository paper settles fixed-separation spectral estimation, not this local-to-Gaussian union-honest length problem. The branchwise converse and removal of \(\Lambda_n\) are open. No matching Pareto boundary or improvement of global union-supremum expected length is claimed.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem records the source-supported Gaussian coordinate on transfer-compatible supplied-fit sequences, with the fuzzy nuisance-product/log and parametric two-point mechanisms proved separately.
statement_notes.gap: The result remains conditional on exact support compatibility and retains \(\Lambda_n\); the frozen core does not prove either unconditional transfer for every supplied fit or the full \(d_n\) coordinate.
statement_notes.consumer: On its stated subexperiment it rules out Gaussian-coordinate expected length below \(d_n^-\), without asserting a global union-supremum improvement or a matching vector frontier.
